scope: Thirteen actual complete public course popups. Exact metadata review, no automatic audit or aliases. Typical offering terms do not guarantee current availability.

ENVS-101.name: Concepts of Environmental Science
ENVS-101.description: Introduces sustainability and environmental problem solving through biodiversity, ecosystems, pollution, energy and climate, with social and engineering context.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course explicitly treats environmental science as the organizing scientific framework, with policy and ethics embedded as supporting interdisciplinary context.

ENVS-111.name: Soil Science
ENVS-111.description: Combines soil taxonomy, ecology, formation, physical properties and conservation with field sampling, laboratory chemistry and spatial analysis.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Soil science and practical field/laboratory investigation are the substantive domain.

ENVS-152H.name: Honors: The Greening of RIT
ENVS-152H.description: Investigates campus sustainability problems and designs responses for energy, waste, transport, land use, stormwater and resource purchasing while considering stakeholders.
ENVS-152H.prerequisites: This class is restricted to students in the Honors program.

category_review.rationale: The stated work is applied environmental planning and campus sustainability problem solving; stakeholder viewpoints frame that practice.

ENVS-250.name: Applications of Geographic Information Systems
ENVS-250.description: Uses GIS software and spatial analysis in domain projects, including project planning, geographic databases and independent applied work.
ENVS-250.prerequisites: Foundational course in student's major field of study or permission of instructor.
notes: Students should be comfortable working with computers; programming experience is described as useful, not a separate required course.

category_review.rationale: The course teaches application of geographic information tools across domains, rather than construction of general database infrastructure or algorithms.

ENVS-305.name: Urban Ecology
ENVS-305.description: Studies urban ecosystems, development impacts and sustainable design through international cases and a required study tour to Malmö.
ENVS-305.prerequisites: Prerequisites: This class is restricted to students with at least 2nd year standing.
notes: Required 2.5-week study tour to Malmö, Sweden after graduation in May; application through the Office of Study Abroad and an additional fee.

category_review.rationale: Ecological functions, ecosystem services and sustainable urban development are the stated disciplinary focus.

ENVS-310.name: Flood Hydrology and Wine Ecology
ENVS-310.description: Examines hydrology, vineyard ecology and climate resilience through environmental and economic models and a required German study tour.
ENVS-310.prerequisites: Enrollment in this course requires permission from the department, as well as approval from RIT Global.
notes: Required 2.5-week study tour to Würzburg, Germany after the spring semester; RIT Global application and an additional fee.

category_review.rationale: Hydrologic and ecological processes and their practical management dominate the described work; model use is domain analysis.

ENVS-531.name: Climate Change: Science Technology & Policy
ENVS-531.description: Surveys atmospheric chemistry, climate modeling, ecological feedbacks, economics, international policy and environmental justice.
ENVS-531.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 3rd year standing.

category_review.rationale: The description intentionally combines natural-science domain content and social/policy analysis without identifying one as dominant.

ESHS-360.name: Sustainable World Water Supply
ESHS-360.description: Combines hydrologic systems and water-supply technologies with health, economic, legal and social consequences of scarcity and climate change.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Physical water systems and supply techniques are substantive alongside regulation and social consequences, supporting a mixed interpretation.

PUBL-531.name: Climate Change: Science, Technology and Policy
PUBL-531.description: Surveys atmospheric chemistry, climate modeling, ecological feedbacks, economics, international policy and environmental justice.
PUBL-531.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 3rd year standing.

category_review.rationale: The course independently repeats a deliberately multidisciplinary science and policy scope; the similar CHEM/ENVS cards do not establish a cross-list identity.

MEDS-250.name: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
MEDS-250.description: Studies nervous, endocrine, skin, muscular and skeletal structure and function through histology, dissection and human physiology experiments.
MEDS-250.prerequisites: Pre-requisite: (BIOL-123 and BIOL-124 and BIOL-125 and BIOL-126) or (BIOL-123 and BIOL-124) or (BIOL-101 and BIOL-102) or (BIOL-121 and BIOL-122) or MEDG-102 or equivalent course or NUTR-BS or NUTRSC-BS students.

category_review.rationale: Organ-system biology and laboratory investigation are explicit medical-science domain content.

MEDS-251.name: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
MEDS-251.description: Studies digestive, cardiovascular, immune, respiratory, excretory and reproductive systems and homeostasis through laboratory investigation.
MEDS-251.prerequisites: Pre-requisite: (BIOL-123 and BIOL-124 and BIOL-125 and BIOL-126) or (BIOL-123 and BIOL-124) or (BIOL-101 and BIOL-102) or (BIOL-121 and BIOL-122) or MEDG-102 or equivalent course or NUTR-BS or NUTRSC-BS students.
notes: The published prerequisite field does not name MEDS-250; a sequence prerequisite is not inferred from the II title.

category_review.rationale: Physiological function and anatomical investigation are medical-science domain content.

CMPE-257.name: Introduction to Quantum Computing and Information Science
CMPE-257.description: Introduces quantum information, cryptography, gates, circuits and algorithms, supported by quantum mechanics and hands-on computing simulators.
CMPE-257.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (PHYS-111 or PHYS-207 or PHYS-211 or PHYS-211A or PHYS-216) and (MATH-172 or MATH-182 or MATH-182A) or equivalent courses.

category_review.rationale: The course centers computational models, algorithms and information protocols; it does not describe artificial-intelligence methods.

MEDS-201.name: Language of Medicine
MEDS-201.description: Teaches medical word construction, terminology, abbreviations, professional writing and translation of medical language into ordinary English.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The actual scope is human communication and specialized language use, rather than clinical anatomy or treatment methods.
